common_name: Black Velvet Gooseberry (Purple-Black Dessert Gooseberry, Blueberry-Flavored Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant dormant bare-root or container stock in fall or early spring in fertile, well-drained soil; Black Velvet crosses European dessert-fruit quality with American disease resistance and is self-fertile, so a single bush sets a full crop.

directions: Black Velvet is a hybrid dessert gooseberry combining European Ribes uva-crispa fruit quality with the vigor and disease resistance of American Ribes hirtellum parentage, selected for its commercial and home-garden potential as a fresh-eating fruit. Ripe berries turn from green through burgundy to a deep purple-black, with a sweet, mild flavor many tasters compare to blueberries rather than the tart bite typical of green or red gooseberries, making it excellent for fresh eating off the bush as well as pies, jams, and desserts. The bush is notably vigorous and disease-resistant, showing good tolerance of powdery mildew and leaf spot compared with older European cultivars, and it is extremely cold-hardy, tolerating temperatures to -40F once dormant. Like other Ribes, it prefers cool summers and consistently moist soil, and benefits from afternoon shade and mulch to keep roots cool in warmer parts of its range; expect reduced vigor and fruit quality in hot, humid summer climates. Prune out the oldest third of canes each winter to renew fruiting wood and improve air circulation through the thorny growth.

common_name: Rexrot Gooseberry (Large-Fruited Mildew-Resistant Red Dessert Gooseberry)

planting.note: Plant dormant bare-root or container stock in fall or early spring in fertile, well-drained soil; Rexrot is a German-bred cultivar valued for heavy yields of large fruit and strong powdery mildew resistance, making it a reliable home-garden and pick-your-own selection.

directions: Rexrot is a large-fruited European gooseberry cultivar from German nursery breeding, prized for heavy, reliable yields and good resistance to powdery mildew, a disease that plagues many older gooseberry cultivars in humid conditions. Fruit is large and round, ripening by midsummer from a yellowish-green base to a red blush on the sun-exposed side, with a rich, aromatic, sweet-tart flavor well suited to fresh eating, pies, and preserves; the high, efficient yield per bush also makes it popular for pick-your-own operations. Like other European gooseberries, Rexrot prefers cool summers and consistently moist, well-drained soil, and benefits from afternoon shade and mulch to keep roots cool where summers run hot and humid; expect diminished vigor in the Deep South and similarly warm, humid climates. Prune out the oldest canes each winter and thin crowded growth to maintain the open framework that keeps mildew pressure low and eases harvest from the thorny wood.
sources: Cornell University Small Fruit Production Guide
Baumschule Horstmann German nursery cultivar catalog
